manual_semantic_audit.method: Every schema-valid item (4/30) and a representative cross-section of schema-invalid items were read by hand against the raw premises/hypothesis. Categories below extend the structural taxonomy with the semantic-failure categories from the phase spec (item 10).

findings.note: Gold True, generated Uncertain. Chain human(x)->mammal(x)->animal(x) translated correctly (real modus-ponens chain, 2-hop), but no premise ever asserts a ground fact matching human(SOMETHING) -- 'occur_in(monkeypox_virus, humans)' does not entail Human(humans) under this schema. The existential hypothesis 'There is an animal' has no witness to instantiate. Partly a genuine hard case: the English relies on 'humans' as an implicit generic reference rather than a stated individual -- borderline ANNOTATION_AMBIGUITY as well as MISSING_PROPOSITION.

Gold False, generated Uncertain. The critical binary relation plays_for(ailton_silva, nautico) was dropped entirely -- premise 3 ('...footballer who plays for Nautico') translated to only footballer(x), losing the relation the hypothesis needs. Compounding failure: the same real-world entity appears as three different IR entity strings across sentences -- 'aitlon_silva' (premise 1), 'aitlon' (premise 2), 'aitlon silva' (premise 3, contains a literal space -- a single logical entity split into 3 unrelated Z3 constants). Also a spelling slip (Ailton -> 'aitlon') carried consistently, which is harmless on its own but compounds the coreference problem.

Gold False, generated Uncertain. Hypothesis 'Ailton Silva does not play for a football club' (a ground fact about one named individual) was translated as forall x (person(x) AND NOT play_for_football_club(x)) -- a universal claim about every person, with a 'person(x)' conjunct that has no basis in the source sentence at all. Both the invented universal quantifier and the invented person(x) predicate are hallucinated structure not present in the English.

'If an object is a hardcover book then it is printed text.' translated to a bare implies(hardcover_book(x), printed_text(x)) with no enclosing forall -- x is used but never bound. This exact pattern (dropping the forall wrapper on an 'If X then Y' universal conditional) recurs in idx 153, 155, 170, 171, 172, 180, 181 -- the single most common individual failure mode in the whole run, despite the prompt's explicit forall-wrapped few-shot example for exactly this sentence shape.

'Tom is not an Osceola wild turkey.' translated to {"type": "predicate", "name": "not", "args": [<nested node>]} -- using "not" as a predicate name taking a full node as an 'argument', instead of the documented {"type": "not", "body": ...} node. Recurs on the very next sentence in the same item (a disjunction wrapped the same wrong way). The schema is understood at the conceptual level (negation is needed and applied to the right content) but not reproduced in the exact required shape.

The long enumerative sentence listing six wild-turkey subspecies produced JSON that was cut off mid-object at the 400-token generation budget, before the closing braces -- invalid_json, but specifically a truncation failure, not a conceptual translation error. This recurs whenever a single sentence has many conjuncts (long enumerations, long disjunctive lists) -- a fixable prompting/budget issue for a future iteration, not a semantic-understanding failure.

cross_cutting_observations: The most common single failure mode (7 of 30 items directly, more indirectly) is dropping the forall wrapper on 'If X then Y' universal conditionals -- QUANTIFIER_ERROR -- despite an explicit matching few-shot example in the prompt.

Entity naming is inconsistent within a single theory even when Qwen is warned to use consistent snake_case entities (idx 199-203: 'aitlon_silva' / 'aitlon' / 'aitlon silva' for one person). This is exactly the predicate/entity-normalization risk flagged in FOLIO_SYMBOLIC_IR.md and normalization.py -- and it is confirmed here as a real, load-bearing failure mode, not a theoretical concern.

Even among the 4/30 items that were fully schema-valid and compiled, 3 of 4 produced 'Uncertain' against a non-Uncertain gold label -- not because the reasoning was wrong, but because key relations were dropped during translation (MISSING_PROPOSITION), so the compiled theory was logically too weak to derive anything. This directly supports the phase's central question: the bottleneck is translation fidelity, not the solver -- solver latency was 0.3-163ms per item against 14s-4797s translation latency.
